attention.description:

oneOf.description: Waiting for the user, e.g. a permission prompt.

oneOf.description: A new workspace named after the file, in the focused window.

tile.description: A browser tile; defaults to the focused tile.

tile.description: A browser tile; defaults to the focused tile.

oneOf.description: Liveness check; replies `pong`.
The whole object model; replies `session`.
Opens a window with one empty workspace.
Records a window's frame after the user moves or resizes it.
Shows or hides a window's workspace sidebar (restored on relaunch).
Every window; replies `windows`.
Workspaces of one window, or of all windows; replies `workspaces`.

Sets the folder whose git branch the sidebar shows; without `path` the

Records the herdr workspace backing a workspace. Sent by the herdr adapter.
Tabs of one workspace, or of all workspaces; replies `tabs`.
Opens a tab with one tile (a terminal unless `content` says otherwise).
Lists tiles; replies `tiles`.
One tile; replies `tile`.

Closes a tile. A terminal's herdr pane is detached, not killed, unless

Focuses a tile; counts as looking at it, so its agent's attention
clears (F11).

Clears a tile's agent attention without moving focus: shells send it
when a focused tile's attention lights up while the user is looking.
Sets or clears a tile's title.
Points a browser tile at `url`; the shell loads it on `tile.updated`.

The shell reports where a browser tile's page is now (after a link,
a redirect, back or forward) and its `<title>`, so `tile.get` and
restore see the live page. Unlike `browser.open` it asks for no load.

Shows `path` in a preview tile. When `tile` is a preview tile it
shows the file and replies `ok`. Any other tile (say, the terminal

A preview tile's rendered content; replies `preview`. Shells call it
when they create a preview view; later changes arrive as

Shows a preview tile's file rendered or as highlighted source (F29);
without `mode` it toggles. Saved per tile.

Lists one folder of a files tile (its root when `dir` is absent);
replies `files`. Doesn't watch it: see `files.expand`.

Lists a folder and watches it from now on: changes arrive as
`files.changed`. Shells send it when the user opens a folder.
Stops watching a folder and the folders open below it.
Points a files tile at another folder.

Opens the folders down to `path` and asks shells to select it
(`files.revealed`).

Shows or hides hidden and gitignored entries; toggles when `show` is
absent. Shells list their open folders again on `files.changed`.

Opens a path from a files tile in a preview tile (the tab's first one,

Closes a files panel and stops watching its folders.
The focused tab's layout; emits `layout.changed` and replies `layout`.
Splits a tile and opens a new one beside it, which takes focus.
Moves focus to the neighbouring tile.
Swaps a tile with its neighbour in `direction`, or with tile `with`.
Moves a tile one step: into its neighbour's slot, or to the tab's edge.
Moves a tile's edge in `direction` by `amount` (negative shrinks).
Zooms a tile to fill its tab; leave `zoomed` out to toggle.

Opens a tile at the end of the tab's stack, whichever tile has focus; a
lone tile becomes master | stack. In a manual tab the stack is evened
out afterwards; in a dynamic tab the tile goes where `[layout] insert`

Swaps a tile with its tab's master (manual tab) or moves it to the
front of the order (dynamic tab); focus stays on the tile.

Toggles master on the left ↔ master on top, keeping the stack's order.
In a Tile tab, `reverse` makes it a quarter turn (absent: toggle;

Gives every tile in the tab's stack the same size.
Switches a tab to a layout kind: `manual` or a dynamic one.

Switches a tab to `kind`, or back to its previous kind if `kind` is
already active.
Steps through the configured cycle of layout kinds.

Adds (or with a negative `delta` removes) masters in a Tile or Three

Grows (positive `delta`) or shrinks the master area of a Tile or Three

Moves a tile `step` places along its dynamic tab's order, wrapping.
Records the herdr pane a terminal tile views. Sent by the herdr adapter.

Gives an ended terminal tile a fresh herdr pane, keeping the tile's id

Reads a terminal's screen or history; replies `text`. History lives in

Scrolls a terminal's view; replies `scroll`. 0 is the live bottom.

Finds lines containing `query` in a terminal's history; replies

Streams events on this connection as `events.event` notifications;

Ends a subscription made on this connection.

A tab or workspace as layout-file TOML; replies `layout_file`.

Every action the palette offers, with its current key chords;

Local plus herdr's saved machines and their connection state;

CommandEntry.description: One entry in the command palette.

action.description:
Keymap action name, when the entry is a keymap action. With `index`
for indexed actions (`switch_tab` + 3).

chords.description: Current bindings on this platform, in config syntax (`cmd+d`).

id.description:
Stable id: the keymap action name (`split_right`, `switch_tab_3`), or
the method name for commands no key is bound to (`browser.open`).

method.description:
The protocol method it sends, if any; `None` for shell-only actions
(palette, sidebar, find…).

needs_tile.description: Acts on the focused tile, so the palette greys it out without one.

planned.description: Not supported yet; shown greyed out.

prompt.description:
Needs input before it can run (a URL, a path, a name): the palette
prompts for `prompt` first.

ConfigDiagnostic.description: A problem in the config file, for the shell's banner.

applied.description: False when the new file had errors: the previous config stays.

Created.description: IDs of what a command created; only the relevant fields are set.

oneOf.description: The request wasn't valid JSON.
Valid JSON, but not a request (e.g. no `method`).
A window, workspace, tab or tile doesn't exist.
The command doesn't apply right now (nothing focused, no neighbour that way…).
Not available in this build or configuration.
A service the command needs (herdr) isn't reachable right now.

Event.description: Something that changed in the core.

oneOf.description: Frame or sidebar changed.
Name, cwd or herdr binding changed.

A workspace's repository or branch changed, or it left a repository
(`git` absent): the sidebar shows the branch (F26). Also visible as
`git` on `workspace.updated`.
A window's workspaces changed order.
A workspace's tabs changed order.
A tile's title or content changed (e.g. a terminal got its herdr pane).

A tile closed. `kill` asks the herdr adapter to kill the terminal's pane
rather than detach from it.

A terminal tile's agent started or stopped needing a look: it became
blocked or finished, or someone focused the tile (F11). Also visible as
`tile.agent.attention` on `tile.updated`.
A tab's tree, focused tile or zoom changed.
The focused window, workspace, tab or tile changed.

A preview tile's file was (re)rendered: on open, on restore and after
every change on disk. Not saved; `preview.get` returns the latest.

Folders a files tile has open changed on disk, or hidden entries were
toggled: list them again. Not saved.

`files.reveal` opened the folders down to an entry: shells expand them
and select it. Not saved.

Git status for a files tile's work tree, after it opens and after
changes. Not saved.

The core's link to herdr came up or dropped. After `connected: true`,
shells reattach terminal tiles that gave up waiting. Not saved.

A herdr machine appeared, changed state or label (ADR 0011). Not
saved.

A herdr machine left herdr's list (removed there, or hidden in
config). Its workspaces stay, unconnected. Not saved.

The agent in a terminal tile changed state, as herdr reports it (F16).
Not saved.

The config file changed on disk and was read again (F25b). When it has
errors the previous config stays and `applied` is false. Not saved.

EventNotification.description: An event plus the subscription it's for: the event's own `event` and `data` fields, and `subscription`.

EventsSubscribe.description:
Parameters of `events.subscribe`. Every filter is optional; together they
narrow the stream (an event must pass all of them).

tile.description:
Only events about this tile: its own `tile.*`, `preview.updated` and
`agent.state_changed` events, layout changes of its tab, and focus
changes to or from it.

workspace.description:
Only events about this workspace: its own events, its tabs' and its
tiles', and `focus.changed` when focus lands in it. Events about no
particular workspace (`herdr.status`, window events) are left out.

FileEntry.description: One entry of a listed folder.

dir.description: A folder, or a symlink to one.

hidden.description: Starts with a dot. Only listed when hidden entries are shown.

ignored.description: Excluded by gitignore rules. Only listed when hidden entries are shown.

FileGitState.description:
A path's git state, for a badge. Folders take the strongest state of the
changes beneath them.

dirs.description: Folders whose entries changed: list them again. Absolute, resolved.

FilesDir.description: A folder of a files tile.

dir.description: Absolute, or relative to the tile's root; the root when absent.

tile.description: A files tile; defaults to the focused tile.

FilesGit.description:
Payload of `files.git`: the git state of every changed path in the
tile's work tree (and the folders above them). Replaces the previous one.

dir.description: The listed folder, absolute and resolved.

entries.description: Folders first, then natural name order (`a2` before `a10`).

root.description: The tile's root, absolute and resolved (symlinks followed).

truncated.description: The folder had more entries than a listing returns; the rest are cut.

path.description: Absolute, or relative to the tile's root.

tile.description:
The files tile the path comes from; defaults to the focused tile. A
files panel (`files.panel`) works too: the path then opens beside the
focused tile. Any other tile is used as the anchor when `path` is
absolute.

oneOf.description:
The tab's first preview tile shows it; without one, a new preview tile
opens to the right of the files tile. Focus stays in the files tile.

A new terminal tile below the files tile, in the folder (a file's
folder for a file). It takes focus.

FilesPanel.description:
A files panel: a file tree outside the layout (the sidebar's Files view).
It answers `files.list`, `files.expand`, `files.collapse`,
`files.reveal`, `files.toggle_hidden` and `files.open` like a files tile,
with its id as `tile`, and its events carry that id.

panel.description: The panel to point at `root`; a new panel when absent.

root.description: The folder to show; `~` expands to the home folder.

path.description:
A file or folder under the tile's root: absolute, or relative to the
tile's root.

dirs.description: The folders to expand, root first.

path.description: The entry to select. Absolute, resolved.

root.description: The folder to show; `~` expands to the home folder.

show.description:
Show (true) or hide (false) hidden and ignored entries; toggles when
absent.

Focus.description: Where the user's focus is. Inner fields are `None` when that level is empty.

Frame.description: A window's frame on screen, in points, origin top left of the main display.

branch.description:
The checked-out branch, or the short commit when `detached`. Absent in
a repository with no commits yet only if git can't name the branch.

detached.description: HEAD points at a commit, not a branch.

dirty.description: Tracked files have changes (untracked files don't count).

HerdrRef.description:
The herdr pane a terminal tile views. Both IDs are kept: herdr changes a
pane's ID when it moves to another workspace, while the terminal ID is what
`herdr terminal attach` takes. The tab ID matters because closing a herdr
tab reports only the tab, and herdr keeps pane and tab IDs (but not the
process) across a server restart.

machine.description:
The herdr machine the pane runs on: `None` for Local, else herdr's
saved-machine ID (ADR 0011). herdr IDs are only unique per server.

base_dir.description:
What relative `cwd` and `path` values in the file resolve against.
Defaults to the file's directory, or the workspace's cwd for `toml`.

path.description: A layout file (`.azulejo.toml`). Give exactly one of `path` and `toml`.

workspace.description: For `new_tab` and `replace_tab`; the focused workspace by default.

step.description: Positions to move through the cycle; negative goes back. Defaults to 1.

path.description:
Also write the file here. Paths in it are made relative to its
directory where they're inside it.

tab.description: Export one tab. Without it, the whole workspace.

workspace.description: The workspace to export; the focused one by default.

LayoutKind.description: How a tab arranges its tiles.

oneOf.description: A split tree edited by hand; the tree is the source of truth.
Masters on one side, a stack on the other.
Every tile full size, the focused one on top.
Masters centred, stacks left and right.

delta.description: Change in the master area's share; negative shrinks. Defaults to 0.05.
How many masters to add; negative removes. Defaults to 1.

step.description: Places to move; negative moves towards the front. Defaults to 1.

LayoutParams.description: Every dynamic kind's parameters, remembered across switches.

amount.description: Share of the enclosing split to move the edge by. Defaults to 0.05.

part.description:
Tile tabs: turn only the master area, so several masters sit side by
side instead of stacked.

reverse.description:
Tile tabs: a quarter turn, anticlockwise when `true`. Absent toggles
master left ↔ top.

content.description: The new tile; defaults to a terminal.

direction.description: Which side of `tile` the new tile goes.

tile.description: The tile to split; defaults to the focused one.

content.description: The new tile; defaults to a terminal.

LayoutState.description:
A tab's layout, as `layout.changed` and `layout.get` report it.

Shells draw from `rects`: every tile's rectangle in the unit square, its
stacking order and whether it's shown (Monocle hides all but the focused
tile without resizing them). `tree` is the tab's split tree: the source of
truth for manual tabs, derived for dynamic ones (ADR 0010).

order.description: Tile order of a dynamic tab, masters first; empty for manual tabs.

params.description: Every kind's parameters, as the tab remembers them.

direction.description: Swap with the neighbour this way. Give exactly one of `direction`, `with`.

with.description: Swap with this tile, which must be in the same tab.

MachineInfo.description: A herdr machine and how Azulejo's link to it is doing.

label.description: What the sidebar shows: "Local", or the label saved in herdr.

message.description: Why it's reconnecting or needs attention, when known.

oneOf.description: Not up yet since Azulejo started.
The link dropped; retrying with backoff.

Retrying won't help (password prompt, host key, no herdr there):
the user fixes it in herdr, e.g. `herdr machine reconnect <label>`.
Not connected on purpose: disabled in herdr or `connect = false`.

Node.description: One node of a layout tree.

ratio.description: Share of the space given to `a`, in (0, 1).

Notification.description:
A message the server sends without being asked, on a connection with a
subscription. On the wire it's a JSON-RPC notification: `method` plus
`params`.

oneOf.description: One event. `event` and `data` are exactly the event's own fields.

The subscriber fell behind and `dropped` events were skipped just
before the next one it receives.

OnExit.description:
What happens to a terminal tile when the process in its pane exits
(`exit`, ctrl+d, a finished command). Config `[terminal] on_exit`; a tile
can override it (layout files' `on_exit`).

oneOf.description: The tile closes, like any terminal window whose shell exits.
The tile stays, ended, offering Respawn or Close.

Orientation.description: Which side the Tile layout's masters sit on.

PaneMeta.description:
What herdr reports about a terminal tile's pane (F28): enough to say what
runs there and where.

command.description:
The command running in the foreground when it isn't the shell, e.g.
`just dogfood`.

cwd.description: The pane's working directory (its foreground process's, when known).

title.description: The title the program in the pane set (OSC 0/2).

Placement.description:
Where one tile goes. `rect` is in the unit square, like
[`Node::rects`]; higher `z` draws on top; hidden tiles keep their rect but
aren't drawn (Monocle's tiles under the top one).

html.description:
A complete HTML document for the tile's webview; absent for native
kinds. When the tile already shows `path`, pass it to
`azulejoPreview.swap(html)` (shared/webview/preview.js) to keep the
scroll position.

mode.description: Rendered, or the file's source highlighted as code (F29).

revision.description:
Counts renders of this tile in this run, so a shell can drop stale
updates.

truncated.description: Only the start of a very large file was rendered.

oneOf.description:
Native kinds: the shell shows `path` with QuickLook (macOS) or GTK
(Linux); there's no `html`.

oneOf.description: Rendered: markdown as a document, images as images.

path.description:

mode.description: Absent toggles between rendered and source.

tile.description: A preview tile; defaults to the focused tile.

oneOf.description: The visible screen.

oneOf.description: Done; nothing to return.

Where a terminal's view sits after `terminal.scroll`.

oneOf.description: The command palette's entries, from `commands.list`.

line.description: 0-based line in the searched history, oldest first.

detached_herdr.description:

closed (detached) tile doesn't come back on the next relaunch. Pruned
once herdr no longer has the pane.

focused_window.description: `None` exactly when there are no windows.

A tab: one layout tree. A tab always holds at least one tile; closing its
last tile closes the tab.

layout.description:
How the tiles are arranged (ADR 0010). Old state files have none and

recent.description:
Recently focused tiles, most recent first: directional focus breaks
ties with it.

tiles.description: The tiles in `root`, in no particular order.

zoomed.description: A zoomed tile fills the tab until unzoomed.

content.description: The tab's first tile; defaults to a terminal.

kind.description: The tab's layout kind, for a subtle hint in the tab bar.

manual.description:

previous.description: The kind before the last switch, for toggling back.

weights.description: Per-tile size weights within a column; absent means 1.0.

workspace.description: Only this workspace's tabs; all when absent.

index.description: New position within its workspace; past the end means last.
